subject: DPA clarifications and follow-up — Acme Payments
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA clarifications and follow-up — Acme Payments

Hi Sonia — great call this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a few follow-ups from our side so your legal team has everything in one place: 

1) Roles: Redwood’s standard position is that customers (Acme) are the Controller and Redwood acts as Processor for customer-provided data sent to the service. If you need language that flips those roles for specific flows, let us know which data types you mean.

2) Subprocessors: We maintain a published list of subprocessors (hosting, monitoring, analytics). We can provide the current list and a process for 30-day notice before adding new subprocessors.

3) Breach notice: Our DPA commits to notifying customers of security incidents affecting customer data. Typical SLA is notification within 72 hours of confirming a material incident — happy to discuss tighter commitments for critical payment data.

4) Data residency: We can route hosted workloads to specific regions (US/EU) and also support Dedicated or Private deployments for strict residency needs. Please confirm whether you require contractual guarantees for EU-only processing for all payment flows.

5) Retention & Logging: Default operational logs retention is 90 days; we offer options to shorten/extend in contract. We capture audit logs (access, API calls) and can provide ephemeral access for audits or periodic exports.

Next steps: I’ve attached our latest DPA (Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf) and would appreciate Acme’s numbered questions. If legal prefers, we can route proposed redlines through DocuSign. We’re happy to jump on a short call with Marissa (legal) to walk through items.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0147
From: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@acme-payments.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Payments Legal <legal@acme-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications and follow-up — Acme Payments

Hi Ben — thanks for the recap and the DPA. I’ve attached a short list of questions from our legal/compliance team (acme_questions.docx) — highlights below: 

- Controller vs Processor: please confirm in writing that Redwood is acting as Processor for customer data and that Acme remains Controller.
- Subprocessors: we need a complete current list and confirmation we’ll receive 30 days’ notice for new subprocessors. If there’s any subprocessor that processes payment data, flag it.
- Breach notice timing: our security team requests a 48-hour notification for any breach affecting payment cardholder data. Can you confirm?
- Data residency: we require EU-only processing for European card transactions under our agreements. Can Redwood guarantee EU-only processing for those flows on the hosted product, or do we need Dedicated/Private?
- Retention & logging: please confirm default retention for audit logs and whether logs containing PII can be limited/removed on request.

Can you loop in Redwood legal and confirm a timeline for answers by end of day tomorrow? We’d like to get this squared away before the pilot kickoff.

Thanks,
Sonia
Sonia Patel
Head of Payments Operations — Acme Payments
sonia.patel@acme-payments.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@acme-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: DPA clarifications and follow-up — Acme Payments

Marissa / Laura — forwarding Acme’s questions (attached acme_questions.docx). Key negotiation points called out by Acme: 48-hour breach notice (they want 48, our standard is 72), EU-only residency for European card transactions (they may require Dedicated/Private or a contractual commitment), and a full subprocessors list with 30-day notice.

Proposed ask: Can we offer a confirmed 48-hour notification for confirmed breaches involving payment data (subject to incident triage/confirmation) while leaving general incident notification at 72 hours? Also propose we provide a signed commitment for routing EU payment processing to the EU region for the pilot if they purchase Dedicated or consent to an addendum for hosted routing.

Marissa — can you review the attached DPA and provide suggested redlines for the 48hr/72hr language, subprocessor notice, and residency clause? Sonia asked for answers by EOD tomorrow — can you reply with a draft for me to send (and copy Acme) by 3pm PT?

Thanks,
Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications and follow-up — Acme Payments

Hi Sonia — thanks for the clear list. I reviewed Ben’s attached DPA (Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf) and responded inline; summary of our positions and proposed edits below. Please consider this a starting point — happy to take a short call to walk through specifics.

1) Roles (Controller vs Processor)
- Confirmation: Redwood will confirm in writing that for customer-submitted data we act as Processor and Acme remains the Controller. We will add explicit language to the DPA restating this relationship.

2) Subprocessors
- We will provide the current subprocessor list and a URL to the live registry. We commit to 30 days’ notice before onboarding new subprocessors.

- If a subprocessor will process payment cardholder data, we will flag that specifically and provide related security attestations.

3) Breach notice / incident communication
- Our standard contract language: Redwood will notify the customer of confirmed security incidents affecting customer data promptly and, where feasible, within 72 hours of confirmation.

- For payment cardholder data (PCI-related incidents) we can commit to a faster escalation path: for confirmed incidents that materially impact payment data we will aim to notify within 48 hours of confirmation and will provide an incident status cadence (initial notification, 24/48/72-hour updates, and a root-cause report).

4) Data residency
- Hosted product: we can route processing to an EU region for EU-only workloads; we will add contractual language to guarantee EU-only processing for specified workflows for the pilot.
- Dedicated/Private: full EU residency guarantees are supported through Dedicated or Private deployments (we will include this option in the quote).

5) Retention & logging
- Default operational/audit log retention is 90 days. We can offer custom retention windows (shorter or longer) as a contract option and can support deletion requests for PII within logs where feasible. For audit purposes, we can provide time-limited access exports.

Next steps: I attached a redlined DPA (Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf, inline comments) and a link to our current subprocessor registry. I can send a DocuSign-ready version with the proposed edits once you confirm the 48-hour commitment for payment-data incidents and whether you want EU routing for the pilot.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/abcdef123456
Subprocessors: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c

If useful, I’m available for a 30-minute call tomorrow morning to finalize language.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security — Redwood Inference
